tasks.title: Engram/PLE: survive the ROCm 7.14 overlapping-host-registration rejection (measured live on this stack 2026-08-31, RUN3-BRIEF §16.1)
tasks.goal: Land the ROCm 7.14 overlapping-host-registration fix on the engram/PLE path. THIS IS MEASURED, NOT HYPOTHETICAL: handoff/RUN3-BRIEF.md §16.1 records that ds4's rocm_host_copy_probe was run inside flashnext:dev on this coordinator on 2026-08-31 and passes ONLY in --expect-overlap-rejected mode, with these exact rows: 'adjacent-malloc range=1 host_register=part or all of the requested memory range is already mapped' followed by 'adjacent-malloc range=1 h2d_copy=invalid argument'. Both halves matter and the second is the one that is easy to miss: after the failed registration, a PLAIN hipMemcpy(H2D) from that same host pointer ALSO fails, so detecting the registration error is not sufficient - the fallback copy must change too. Read §15.1 for the mechanism: the registration is PAGE-ROUNDED (base rounded down, length rounded up), so two logically DISJOINT tensor slices of one mmap collide whenever their rounded spans touch or abut. With a ~51.2 GB engram table sliced into many non-page-aligned spans this is the COMMON case, not an edge case. Reference implementation to port by shape, not by copy: ~/Downloads/ds4-strix-halo-tp-odinlink rocm/ds4_rocm_runtime.cuh:5513-5600 (cuda_model_range_ptr, commit 8d45d16); §15.1 of the brief quotes the exact fallback loop. Three properties of that fix are load-bearing and must survive the port: the pinned bounce exists ONLY on the overlap error path so the ordinary path pays nothing; it is CAPPED at 64 MiB regardless of tensor size so extra RSS is bounded; and it is freed on success AND on every error exit. Also guard the second, silent failure mode at :5548 - cudaErrorNotSupported or cudaErrorInvalidValue latching a 'mapping unsupported' flag PERMANENTLY disables the zero-copy path for the whole process; log loudly if that latch is ever set. Prefer page-ALIGNING the slices where the code allows it: §16.1 records that the probe's page-aligned-register and anonymous-mmap-register cases both pass cleanly, so alignment is a real mitigation and not merely a bounce. WHERE THE CODE LIVES: the engine is the fork mecattaf/vllm branch flashnext, not this repo; patches/ is a MIRROR of that branch (patches/MANIFEST.md: 'These patches are provenance and review artifacts, not build inputs'), and scripts/verify-fork.sh enforces n_patches >= n_commits against the live branch. So the work is: clone or update the fork at $FN_FORK_DIR (default $HOME/.cache/flashnext/vllm-fork), make the change in the ple_mmap registration path, run the fork's own tests for that module, commit and PUSH to branch flashnext, then mirror that commit into this repo as patches/0013-<slug>.patch with a MANIFEST.md row in the established grammar. The push is what cp-build picks up; the patch file is the durable record and the only thing this lane commits here. If the push cannot be completed, say so explicitly in your final message rather than mirroring a patch that does not exist upstream - a mirror that lies breaks verify-fork.sh for every later task. Boundaries: touch only patches/.
deliveredBehaviors: A page-adjacent registration collision on the engram mmap no longer fails the model load
The 64 MiB pinned bounce exists only on the overlap path and is freed on every exit

tasks.title: Receipts survive the lane worktree, and the closing gate stops confusing 'nothing ran' with 'everything passed' (RUN3-BRIEF §18.3, §2.1)
tasks.goal: Make checkpoint evidence survive the night. THIS IS WHY TWO GREEN NIGHTS BANKED ZERO ENGINE EVIDENCE and it is the highest-leverage task in this campaign. Read handoff/RUN3-BRIEF.md §18.3 first - it was read from the tally source at 62fac87 and it rules out the obvious fix. The mechanism: a checkpoint task is contractually forbidden from carrying conflictDomains (tally.nix crates/tally-core/src/campaign_contract.rs:473, 'checkpoint task {id} must not carry conflictDomains'), so a checkpoint owns no paths and NOTHING it writes is ever committed; it runs in a lane worktree that is then discarded. Checkpoint purity is checked with 'git status --porcelain --untracked-files=no' (crates/spec-build-driver/src/actions.rs:4794-4806), so only TRACKED changes are refused - an untracked receipt is perfectly legal, it simply dies with the worktree. scripts/receipt-restore.py already solves the other half (a re-run restamps ts and dirties a TRACKED receipt, which fails purity) and its own docstring notes that new untracked receipts are never touched. THE FIX, in two parts. (1) Every receipt writer must ALSO write its receipt to a durable absolute path OUTSIDE any worktree: $FN_STATE_DIR/receipts/<step>.json, where FN_STATE_DIR is already bind-mounted into the containers at the same path on both nodes (host/fn-cluster-up.sh:83 and :98), so this works from inside the serve container at no cost. Write the durable copy FIRST and the in-repo copy second, so a crash between them loses the disposable one. Make it idempotent and never let a failure to write the durable copy fail the step itself. (2) Fix the blind closing gate: scripts/receipts-verify.py exits 0 on '3 receipts checked, 0 violations' because MISSING receipts are legal, so it cannot distinguish 'nothing ran' from 'everything passed' - verified again on 2026-08-31 with 3 receipts on disk against 13 pre-declared. Add an EXPECTED-SET assertion: a --require <step,step,...> or --expect-set mode that fails when a named receipt is absent, defaulting OFF so the existing gate argv keeps passing unchanged, and have it read both results/receipts/ and $FN_STATE_DIR/receipts/ so a receipt that survived only in the durable location still counts. Keep the results/receipts/failed/ quarantine behaviour exactly as it is (D12): one graded failure must not redden every later gate run. Cover all of it in tests/test_receipt_durability.py, including the case that matters - a receipt present ONLY in the durable location satisfies the expected set. Boundaries: touch only scripts/receipts-verify.py, scripts/receipt-restore.py, and tests/test_receipt_durability.py.
deliveredBehaviors: A checkpoint receipt survives the discarding of its lane worktree
The receipts gate can be asked to assert an expected set and fails on an absent receipt
The existing gate argv keeps passing unchanged with the assertion defaulted off

tasks.title: Fourth fn_* instrument: the all-reduce timer, without which 'decode is allreduce-dominated' cannot be evaluated by any artifact in this repo (RUN3-BRIEF §10.1, §13.7)
tasks.goal: Add the all-reduce timer as a fourth fn_* instrument in the container overlay, alongside fn_synctrace.py, fn_offload_batch.py and fn_expert_union.py, following their established shape (container/rootfs/ is COPYed into site-packages by container/Containerfile:117, so a new module there is importable without touching the fork). WHY THIS IS NOT OPTIONAL: handoff/RUN3-BRIEF.md §10.1 records that without it, the A/B criterion 'the bench shows decode is allreduce-dominated' CANNOT BE EVALUATED BY ANY ARTIFACT IN THIS REPO. Wrap the communicator's all_reduce and log three things, per §13.7 - and the first two are what separate 'the custom path was inert' from 'the custom path was slow', which §13.1 shows is the exact failure mode that would otherwise make a whole arm measure nothing: (a) a fired/declined counter for any custom path, (b) torch.cuda.is_current_stream_capturing() sampled AT THE CALL SITE, and (c) staging time split from wire time, because without the split the write-combining staging trap of §13.6 is invisible. Bucket by layer type: this model is heterogeneous, 12 QSA full-attention layers and 36 GDN layers, and an aggregate number hides which one pays. Follow §14.15 step 1 - measure the collective's split on the STOCK RCCL/TCP arm, three perf_counter reads per collective (detect, exchange, compute-between). The equivalent measurement on the only production gfx1151 two-node TP deployment OVERTURNED ITS AUTHORS' OWN LEADING HYPOTHESIS: they were certain the gate lockstep dominated and it was 11% transport against 88% own-GPU compute (§14.1). If our split resembles theirs we learn it in 30 minutes instead of spending the night on transport. Non-negotiable mechanics: the instrument must be OFF unless explicitly enabled by a named env kill switch, it must add no measurable cost when off, it must never raise into the serve path (wrap every read in a try/except that degrades to not recording), and it must write its summary through the same receipt discipline the rest of the campaign uses so cp-bench can read it. Use perf_counter and do NOT insert any device synchronisation to get a timing - a sync in the decode loop changes the thing being measured, and §14.6 records a documented non-deterministic stall from exactly that mistake. Cover it in tests/test_allreduce_instrument.py with a fake communicator. Boundaries: touch only container/rootfs/ and tests/test_allreduce_instrument.py.
deliveredBehaviors: Per-collective detect/exchange/compute timings bucketed by QSA and GDN layer type
A fired/declined counter and the capture state sampled at the call site
Off by default, no device synchronisation added to the decode loop

acceptanceCriteria.description: The instrument is covered against a fake communicator.

tasks.title: TP=2 fails loudly and early: swap-proxy arbitration, the eight parity assertions, and selection-time expert sharding on both MoE paths (RUN3-BRIEF §15.4, §14.5)
tasks.goal: Harden the TP=2 path so first light fails LOUDLY and EARLY rather than silently wrong, and so nothing races it. This lane AUTHORS ONLY - cp-tp2 executes. Four things. (1) SWAP-PROXY ARBITRATION, the newly identified race: the local model-swap proxy service (the always-on Go proxy that fronts the single-node model pool and listens on port 9292; resolve its systemd unit name with `systemctl list-units '*swap*'` rather than hardcoding it) holds no GPU at rest (measured idle: /running empty, 525 MB VRAM which is the desktop), but it spawns a backend process on ANY request to :9292 - and that port has two live doors, the tailnet and the house LAN, plus a local utility-model wrapper. A swap-in landing mid-serve allocates out of the same 125 GB unified pool vLLM is holding. NOTHING ARBITRATES THIS: host/fn-cluster-up.sh contains zero references to that proxy or to :9292 and the two systems are mutually blind. Add an explicit stop of that unit on BOTH twins before the serve and a restart in the teardown path, including on the failure exit - a stop, never a disable - and record in the receipt whether it was running when we arrived so the morning can tell. (2) PARITY AND DIVISIBILITY ASSERTIONS, all eight of RUN3-BRIEF §15.4, fail-closed, BEFORE the first TP=2 launch. The precedent is exact: the reference implementation computes n_groups/2 with no parity check, so an odd head count silently drops a group. The highest-risk item for OUR config is the SHARED EXPERT: we have 512 routed experts top-10 plus 1 shared, and 1 is ODD and cannot be range-split - decide and assert explicitly whether it is replicated and folded exactly once or K-split so the sum reconstructs it. This is the item that produces FLUENT WRONG OUTPUT: their defect dropped the shared expert from every decode layer and the text stayed plausible. Also assert QSA n_heads and n_kv_heads are even so GQA groups do not straddle a rank boundary, that any slice boundary is a multiple of the FP8 block size (a misaligned slice mixes neighbouring blocks' scales and is SILENTLY WRONG), and that both ranks derive the same gate schedule from TENSOR PRESENCE rather than layer index, given the heterogeneous 12 QSA / 36 GDN layout. (3) EXPERT SHARDING, §14.5: shard at SELECTION, not by masking weights after it - masking requires every expert to be addressable and therefore contradicts a rank holding only half, which is what produced their 'arena alloc failed for moe_gate' then illegal memory access. Check BOTH the prefill and decode MoE paths: their first fix touched only the one-token entry point and prefill went unsharded, which they record would have been 'silently wrong'. Predict per-rank residency offline from the checkpoint header BEFORE loading and assert it, which converts a class of OOM debugging into arithmetic, and assert DISTINCT per-rank shard checksums as a one-line proof the ranks own different halves. (4) Keep TRITON_CACHE_DIR and TORCHINDUCTOR_CACHE_DIR pinned exactly as they already are - host/fn-cluster-up.sh:59-61 generates the env file through ENV_FILTER which already includes TORCHINDUCTOR_ and TRITON_, and :83/:98 bind-mount FN_STATE_DIR at the same path on both nodes. That is CORRECT TODAY; verify it, do not rewrite it. Do not perform a live serve in this lane. Boundaries: touch only host/ and scripts/run-tp2.sh.
deliveredBehaviors: The swap proxy is stopped on both twins for the serve and restarted on every exit path
All eight parity and divisibility assertions fail closed before the first launch
Expert sharding happens at selection on both the prefill and decode paths

This is the ONLY task permitted to write results/receipts/, and it runs last for exactly that reason - see RUN3-BRIEF §18.3. Copy every receipt from the durable location $FN_STATE_DIR/receipts/ into results/receipts/, preserving results/receipts/failed/ quarantine records as quarantine records rather than promoting them, then run scripts/receipts-verify.py over the assembled set and commit. Do not invent, edit, backfill or reformat a receipt: if a step never ran, its receipt is ABSENT and that absence is the finding - the whole point of the expected-set assertion is that a missing receipt is loud, so a collector that manufactures one destroys the evidence it exists to preserve. Write results/receipts/INDEX.md: one row per expected step naming the receipt path, whether it landed, where it came from (durable location, in-repo, or absent), and for anything absent or in failed/, one plain sentence on what that means for the morning. Do not grade the campaign in that file and do not editorialise about success - state what is there. Boundaries: touch only results/receipts/.
